result.summary: This unit is the surface of go.opentelemetry.io/otel v1.33.0's attribute and codes packages: pure in-memory types for telemetry key/value attributes and status codes, with JSON and string encoding. I checked for init code, build steps, embedded payloads, runtime hooking, and network, file or exec use, and found none. The flagged NETWORK and ARBITRARY_EXECUTION capabilities come from reflection and fmt/json interface dispatch.

findings.title: Pure data-type library with no side effects
findings.detail: The attribute and codes packages match upstream OpenTelemetry v1.33.0. They contain no init functions, no build-time code, no cgo or assembly, and no encoded or embedded data. The packages do no file, network or process access. type_string.go is ordinary stringer output.

capabilities.explanation: Comes from reflection and dynamic dispatch, not loaded code. set.go uses reflect.ValueOf, reflect.New and reflect.ArrayOf to build fixed-size arrays of KeyValue so that attribute sets are comparable. value.go IntSliceValue does the same for int64 arrays. Calls through encoding/json and fmt to interface methods (Stringer, MarshalJSON) are also flagged. Nothing is loaded or run from data.

No network code in this package. The capability is a conservative call-graph artifact: fmt.Sprint, json.Marshal and the Stringer(k, v fmt.Stringer) helper in kv.go call interface methods that Capslock cannot resolve, so it includes net types' String or MarshalJSON methods. Nothing here opens connections.

Comes from json.Unmarshal into interface{} and from fmt.Errorf/Sprintf in Code.UnmarshalJSON and MarshalJSON. These use reflection and interface dispatch internally. No code is loaded or executed from data.

No network use. This is a call-graph artifact of fmt and encoding/json interface dispatch (Stringer/Marshaler methods that might belong to net types). The package only converts status codes to and from strings and JSON.
